summary: Google authors compare two agents on the same harness and model (Gemini 3 Flash): a baseline that writes tests directly vs a 'Spec-Driven' agent that first writes a semi-formal .spec.md of pre/post-conditions and undefined behaviors per API, then generates tests from it. On 90 single-file historical bug fixes from Google's monorepo (C++, Java, Python, Go), tests are generated greenfield against the fixed code and judged by whether they fail on the reverse-patched buggy code.

claims.claim: Spec-driven agent improves bug detection by 9.8 pp (p=0.0352).
claims.evidence: Table 2: detect@5 63.2% [53.3,73.3] vs 53.4% [43.3,63.3]; McNemar p=0.0352 at k=4 and k=5 only. At k=1 the gain is +4.2 pp, p=0.3075 (not significant); k=2 p=0.4545. Abstract reports the best-k figure. Unique detections at k=5: 12 vs 3 (45 shared).

claims.claim: Spec-driven agent improves branch coverage by 2.5 pp (p=0.0034).
claims.evidence: Table 3: branch 48.9% vs 46.4% (Wilcoxon p=0.0034); line coverage 74.4% vs 74.8% (n.s.). Small effect with overlapping CIs.

claims.claim: Spec-driven tests are judged superior to baseline in 77.8% of cases and to developer-written tests in 56.7%.
claims.evidence: Fig. 2/3; judge is Gemini 3.1 Pro with 5-vote majority, self-agreement >=90%. No human validation of the judge; judge rubric was itself LLM-condensed from internal docs; same vendor model family as the agent.

claims.claim: Capturing the violated contract in the spec predicts bug detection.
claims.evidence: §5.3.1: 54.9% (151/275) detection with contract coverage vs 19.4% (34/175) without; Fisher p=3.62e-14, phi=0.35. Contract coverage itself is LLM-judged, with the judge given bug description and fix diff.

claims.claim: Spec-driven generation costs ~38% more tokens, ~16% more tokens per unique bug found.
claims.evidence: Table 4: 336.7M vs 243.9M total tokens; 5.9M vs 5.1M per unique bug detected.

patterns.note: Writing an explicit intermediate spec before tests gives a modest but significant gain at k>=4 on real industrial bugs; note the spec is extracted from existing (fixed) code, not authored ahead of implementation.
Structured pre/post-conditions + test suggestions act as acceptance criteria; contract coverage correlates with detection (phi=0.35).
Uses LLM-as-judge for quality and for contract coverage; reliability shown only as self-agreement, not against humans.
Proposes an optional human spec-curation step but deliberately bypasses it in the evaluation.
Both agents have a run_test tool; validity enforced by post-run audit discarding runs that touch source.
Evaluation on real production bugs from an industrial monorepo rather than public benchmarks.
Reports token overhead of the spec phase explicitly.

methodology.sample: 90 historical bug-fixes from Google's internal issue tracker, single production file per fix; 5 runs per bug (450 runs); 83 suites in qualitative analysis.
methodology.baselines: Same-harness direct test-generation agent (fair, controlled comparison, but no external test-generation tools or other agent baselines).
methodology.models: Gemini 3 Flash for both agents (temperature 1.0); Gemini 3.1 Pro as judge. Single model family.
methodology.variance: k=5 runs; bug-level bootstrap 95% CIs; McNemar and Wilcoxon tests. Good.
methodology.ablations: None beyond baseline-vs-spec; HITL step not evaluated; no ablation of spec components (pre/post vs suggestions).
methodology.contamination_controls: Internal monorepo bugs reduce public-training exposure; authors argue same-model comparison neutralizes contamination (weak argument, since contamination could interact with the prompting strategy).
methodology.languages: C++, Java, Python, Go (no per-language breakdown reported).

standards.peer_review: To appear at SpecOps 2026 workshop (co-located with SPLASH 2026).
standards.artifacts: None: internal Google dataset, no code or prompts link found.

biases.detail: Only Gemini 3 Flash as agent and Gemini 3.1 Pro as judge; acknowledged in §6.
Qualitative superiority (77.8%, 56.7%) and Contract Coverage rely on an LLM judge validated only by self-agreement, with no human-agreement study; failure taxonomy also LLM-labelled.
Abstract headline +9.8 pp and p=0.0352 is reported at k=5; single-attempt gain (+4.2 pp) is not significant, and this is not mentioned in the abstract.
Internal dataset and harness; not reproducible outside Google.
Specs are extracted from the already-fixed code, so the agent describes correct behavior; in real use specs would be derived from possibly buggy code or written up front.
Claims 'parity with human-level engineering rigor' from an LLM judge preference of 56.7%.

coi.vendor_products_evaluated: Gemini 3 Flash (agent) and Gemini 3.1 Pro (judge), both Google models; Google internal codebase.
coi.detail: The comparison is between two prompting strategies on the same Google model, so the main claim does not directly promote a product; but the vendor's own model family judges its own model's output, and nothing is independently replicable.

verdict_reason: One of the few controlled, statistically tested industrial comparisons of a spec-first agent step, but effects are modest and only significant at k>=4. It uses a single model family, qualitative claims rest on an unvalidated same-vendor LLM judge, and nothing is released.
applicability: Directly relevant to the Java team's spec-driven rollout. A cheap, host-agnostic harness step is supported: have the agent write a per-class .spec.md of pre/post-conditions and undefined behavior (for example, ingestion parsers' handling of missing fields, malformed content, and versioned schemas) before generating JUnit tests. Expect roughly 38% more tokens and a gain that is real but modest; it appears mainly with multiple attempts (k>=4). The spec file is a plain committed artifact, so it works across mixed hosts and fits a spec-driven development workflow. The evidence covers single-file fixes in one monorepo, so it says nothing about cross-repo contracts between the 4+ ingestion repos. Keep the human spec-review step the paper skipped, since 141 of 450 runs failed because the spec missed the contract (missing error handling, omitted methods).

conflicts_with.detail: Same batch: TDD-Agent finds test-first alone (one round) adds only ~1.5-2.9 pts and that self-generated oracles converge to consistent-but-wrong states; this paper reports a significant gain from an explicit spec step, but its own failure analysis (110 test-generation failures, 141 spec failures) shows the same oracle-incompleteness problem.
